correctness.rationale: For every \(p\ge p_a\), the separated Hamilton--Jacobi potentials remain admissible because the square-root branch has the same sign pattern on negative and positive products. Their endpoint difference is \(F_n(a,p)\), giving a calibration upper bound. Direct differentiation yields \(\partial_pF_n=2\Psi_n\), and the positive kernel strictly decreases with \(p\), hence \(F_n\) is strictly convex. The source's sign change of \(\Psi_n(a,p_a)\) gives the phase transition at \(a_n\). In the post-closing regime, \(\Psi_n(a,p)\) increases from a negative value to \(\log(1/a)>0\), so there is a unique root. The characteristic formulas show that this root makes the reflected contact points coincide at \((\sqrt a,-\sqrt a)\); calibration then attains the bound. The endpoint \(a=1\) is forced onto two axis-aligned boundary segments and has zero action. Uniform large-momentum expansions give the stated endpoint constants. No finite experiment is used as proof.

value.rationale: The source singles out the post-closing fixed-turning problem as a genuine auxiliary variational problem and explicitly leaves it undeveloped. The result gives its complete one-dimensional optimization mechanism, proves that the momentum is uniquely selected, constructs the sharp cornered maximizer, and determines the exact degeneration rate as the turning constraint approaches the boundary. This is a natural structural refinement of the source's calibration theory rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
